pools.ruling: Colour, not scoped: the roster's character, guaranteed by the key.

lines.text: {settlement} keeps a court and keeps a place for those the court is finished with, which means the town has decided its quarrels are its own business to settle.
{settlement} is administered, visibly: rules here have rooms, and the rooms have officers.
In {settlement} the law is a building you can point to, and the pointing settles a certain number of arguments on its own.

keyGuarantees: a paid standing force: hasMilitaryInst, hasNavy or hasWatch (no court+prison); not reducible to one atom, so prose
pools.ruling: Not scoped: keeping professionals "for its safety" names a purpose, not a calm; line 2 presumes stone defences.

lines.text: Armed order is part of {settlement}'s furniture; the town keeps professionals for its safety rather than trusting to luck and neighbours.
{settlement} pays for its own defense in wages, not only in stone, and the paying is a standing decision renewed every season.

pools.ruling: Colour, not scoped: the roster's character.

lines.text: {settlement} supports work that only towns of a certain seriousness support, and the seriousness rubs off on the rest of the place.
There are people in {settlement} whose whole trade is knowing things, and the town has decided it can afford them.

keyGuarantees: hasGranary or hasHospital (none of the earlier antecedents)
pools.ruling: Not scoped: provision is a building, not a plenty claim; line 1 presumes both stores and care, line 2 the granary.

lines.text: {settlement} keeps stores against the bad season and care for the bad year; the town has met scarcity before and built its answer into the roster.
A town does not keep a granary out of optimism; {settlement}'s provision is the polite form of its memory.

pools.ruling: Colour, not scoped: a thin roster asserts no calm.

lines.text: {settlement} keeps few institutions because it needs few; what a larger town does with buildings, this one does with acquaintance.
Nothing in {settlement} is official that could instead be somebody's job on the side.
